title: Pulling-Away Check
concept: A short, honest count to tell needing space apart from pulling away — so you know which repair to reach for. It describes behaviour you can both see, never your partner’s intent.
whenToUse: When dinner is all logistics and the last real question was weeks ago. If contempt has taken the place of frustration, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first.
steps: Each of you marks, on your own, which of the eight signs (listed under Practise) you’ve noticed, then compare notes. Describe behaviour you’ve seen — don’t claim to know the other person’s intent.
If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first. The same goes for fear or coercion at any count.
None of these? Good. Keep up the daily floor. One or two signs: you likely need some space and a few small repairs (Micro-Repair, Morning + Evening Rhythm).

Three or more signs: one or both of you may be pulling away. Bring back the daily floor and your check-ins for two weeks; if nothing has shifted, book a Full Recovery conversation. Drift is nobody’s fault, but you can each name your part. A specific breach of trust goes to Trust Recovery.
Set a time window to check whether you’re both leaning back in.

phrases.text: I’m noticing some distance. Do you just need space, or is something bigger going on?
I want a Full Recovery conversation. Can we book it for when we’re both calm?
If contempt has crept in, I think we need outside help.

working: A ticks three signs and B ticks four. Both tick the same three: fewer non-logistical check-ins, mostly practical conversations, repairs that feel routine. They bring back the daily floor and their morning and evening check-ins for two weeks. Nothing has shifted, so they book a Full Recovery conversation and keep the check-ins up for 21 days, looking back once a week.
notWorking: The weekends have gone quiet, and A decides to say nothing and wait for B to notice. A month goes by with nothing booked, and the quiet starts to feel normal.
activity: Mark the signs on your own, then compare. Check monthly, or weekly if you’re worried. The eight signs: (1) fewer non-logistical check-ins, (2) less curiosity about each other, (3) avoiding future plans, (4) doing more on your own in place of shared time (time apart is healthy), (5) mostly practical conversations, (6) going-through-the-motions affection, (7) repairs that feel routine, (8) contempt instead of frustration. If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first. Then use the steps above to see what your count means.
warn: If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first. Fear or coercion at any count: stop; safety and outside support come first. This is a way to start a conversation, not a verdict or a score to hold against anyone: describe what you’ve seen, and wanting time alone or plans of your own isn’t a sign by itself.
note: Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this protocol, not a failure of it.
